test/access.test.js allPages() lists M2, M3, M4, both M7 variants, M6, M8, the unknown path and a first-time M1 through a real POST, each with its expected status and title.
test/access.test.js:115 now covers the empty shelf through a second real server with status 200, title and the empty message.

findings.text: Mutation smoke reports T-29 as survived. This is expected and is not a weak witness: the unit's production diff adds only a wrapping rule and an aria-label, and never touches the palette or lettering declarations that T-29 protects. T-29 preserves an existing look, and direct mutations of those declarations turn it red.

experiments.command: for each of --paper, --ink, --rust, --letter: sed the value in public/style.css; node --test --test-name-pattern='T-29' test/access.test.js; git checkout public/style.css. Then the same with the h2 and h1 font-family lines removed.

findings.text: This limit is unchanged and stays a note: rule() reads only the first rule for a selector, so a later overriding rule leaves T-29 green. The builder chose not to take it up, which is acceptable because the current stylesheet has no such override and A4 holds.

experiments.command: printf '\nh2 { font-family: sans-serif; }\n' >> public/style.css; node --test --test-name-pattern='T-29' test/access.test.js; git checkout public/style.css

debt.drag: A later unit could override the look or the tap-target rules further down the stylesheet without any test going red.

reasons: Prior directives and R-15 are resolved. The empty-shelf page is rendered through a second real server on a temporary data file and runs checkPage with status 200, its title and the empty message. Replacing the empty-shelf paragraph with a skipped heading, an unlabelled input, a second h1 or nothing each turns only that test red; I restored the file each time. R-16 and R-17 were released notes and remain notes.

Regression review: the only change since the last gate is test/access.test.js. The checkPage refactor keeps the assertions, and the `return` for the unknown path replaces a `continue` that was the last statement of the loop, so behaviour is the same. The full suite passes 84/84 on Node 26.13.0 in this checkout.

A1 pass: at 360x640 in Chromium, on desktop and mobile emulation, every page had scrollWidth 360. That covers M1 to M8, the b1 pages, a 300-character q and 100 CJK characters; the empty shelf ran on desktop emulation only.

A2 pass: keyboard alone operated search, all seven Reserve links and the form through M4 and autofocus to the confirmation. Focused controls showed a solid 3px rgb(43,38,32) outline, and no target was under 44px.
A3 pass: test/access.test.js proves the checkable markup on every page, and the accessibility tree shows the refusal first in main.

A4 pass: T-29 is present and goes red on direct mutation. Screenshots show paper, ink, rust, dashed rules and a single column, with no card grid or app chrome. Hand lettering could not be seen in this environment, so the walk's V-11 judgement should be made knowing that.
Non-goals hold: the diff adds no JavaScript, dependency, palette change or new visible copy.

premises.claim: The empty-shelf branch is now reached by the access test through the running server.
